title: Arrays of records and field-based search
goal: Find a record by its id field, distinguish an unknown identifier from zero quantity, and stay inside array bounds.

prerequisites.text: Know structure members and zero-based array indices.
Know how to check a pointer against NULL before reading a member.

terms.title: Lookup key
terms.definition: The field value used to find a record. For deliveries this is the identifier; the quantity is record data.

terms.title: Record count
terms.definition: The number of existing elements. With count = 3, valid indices are 0, 1 and 2.

terms.title: No result
terms.definition: A NULL pointer means there was no match. A matching record can still contain a quantity of zero.

sections.title: Search knows where the array stops
paragraphs: The workshop stores tools under IDs 17, 23 and 42. The number 23 is not an index: it is the key on position 1.

Search compares only the id of each record. The condition i < count keeps the index in bounds when count matches the number of accessible records. Compute the length where the array itself is visible. A parameter declared as tools[] receives a pointer, and sizeof on that parameter cannot give the element count.
The function returns the address of a matching element or NULL. The array in main stays alive until main ends. const makes the matching pointer suitable for reading the record.

sections.title: One key is found and the other is absent
paragraphs: Before running, mark which element find checks first and how many it examines for 30.
steps: For key 23 compare 17 and 23. At the second comparison, return the address of tools[1].
Check the returned pointer. It is not NULL, so reading and printing 23 and 5 is valid.
For key 30 check 17, 23 and 42. After the loop return NULL and print missing without reading members.

sections.title: Locate and check the defect
paragraphs: If the last identifier is missed, trace i and count. With four records, index 3 is valid. In the exercise, read result->id only after a lookup returns the address of a record. Dereferencing NULL has undefined behavior. Locate the error in the source without running that variant.
A Clang const-qualified type diagnostic points to an attempt to write through a pointer to const data. Keep this function read-only instead of casting const away.

sections.title: Change, predict and check
paragraphs: Change the first example key to 42, then to 17. Count comparisons before a match and consider what changes if the records are reordered.
If keys repeat, this code returns the first match. Define identifier uniqueness as a separate contract. The next lesson rejects a duplicate before changing the array.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Review the language constructs used in the worked example.

selfcheck.prompt: What is the result of looking up 23?
feedback: 23 is a record key at index 1.
The tool ID is not converted into an index.
The array contains a record with id 23.

selfcheck.prompt: What should be printed for a matching key 54 whose quantity is 0?
feedback: missing applies only when there is no such record.
Zero quantity is valid data for an existing record.
54 is in the allowed identifier range.

selfcheck.prompt: What does find return when count = 0, and why does it never read the first element?
selfcheck.feedback: NULL. At i = 0, the expression 0 < 0 is false, so the loop body does not run.

practice.title: Delivery lookup
practice.task: The log has four records: 12 → 8, 31 → 3, 54 → 0, 77 → 26. The first line, up to 63 bytes, contains one integer ID in 1–9999. Complete the search by id. Print the ID and quantity separated by a space on a match. Print missing for a valid absent ID. Print invalid for malformed input or an out-of-range number.

cases.label: Zero quantity on a matching record

criteria: 12 and 77 are found at opposite ends of the array. 54 prints as 54 0. 99 yields missing and 0 yields invalid.
The caller passes the actual array length. Search indexes only while i < count, and members are read through a valid pointer to a record.
practice.hint: Do not compare quantity with the key. The matching pointer and the quantity member answer different questions.

steps.why: The search indexes the array but compares the key with a named member.
These cases distinguish zero quantity from no result.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: Add delivery {80, 77} to your own list. Predict the results for 77 and 80 with the correct comparison and with the original mistake.
criteria: Correct lookup leaves 77 26 for 77 and yields 80 77 for 80. Explain why looking up quantity would pick a different record.
